Artists Space presents *Multiple Offerings*, the first retrospective in twenty-five years dedicated to the groundbreaking work of the artist Theresa Hak Kyung Cha. She produced an expansive range of works comprising performances for film and video, installation, photography, artist’s books (including her genre-defying book *Dictée* from 1982), and works on paper, which will fill Artists Space’s entire first floor. In her lifetime, Cha contributed to experimental art scenes in New York City, San Francisco, Paris, and beyond. Her work has had a quietly profound influence on subsequent generations of artists.

…

On November 5, 1982, Cha’s short but prolific career came to an end when she was murdered just weeks before her planned exhibition at Artists Space. On Saturday, November 14, join us for an opening event celebrating the Shifting Grounds group exhibition. During the opening event, artist Maya Ojalvo Oren will present *The Table as the Altar*, a participatory performance inspired by her family’s daily ritual of coffee and cookies. Passed down from her Turkish grandparents, the ritual centers on gathering around the table every afternoon, after the siesta, to share Turkish coffee and simit.
